references.text: Nathanael confirms Jesus' divine identity with the titles 'Son of God' and 'King of Israel', which mirrors Mary's confession of Jesus as the Son of God.

In his high priestly prayer, Jesus himself defines 'eternal life' as knowing him as 'the only true God' and 'the one you have sent, Jesus Christ', directly linking the title 'Christ' to the Son of God and his coming into the world.
John explains the purpose of his gospel: that readers may believe that Jesus is 'the Christ, the Son of God', and by believing receive life in his name, which is the core of Mary's confession.
Peter's confession in Matt 16:16 uses almost identical wording: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God', as a direct answer to Jesus' question about who he is.
The term 'the one coming into the world' (ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος) in Mary's confession is a direct reference to the incarnate Logos who 'became flesh and dwelt among us' in the Gospel of John.
Peter confesses in the same way as Mary: 'We have believed and know that you are the Holy One of God', linking faith to Jesus as the one who has the words of God.
